chapter.name: Measuring Space: Perimeter and Area
chapter.blurb: Perimeter and the circumference of a circle, pi, arc length, areas of plane figures, Heron and Brahmagupta formulas, and the area of a circle and sector.

scope_in.item: Perimeter of squares, triangles, rectangles; the C/D ratio and C = 2 pi r
Pi: historical approximations, Madhava's series, and pi is irrational
Length of an arc, perimeter of sectors and shapes with arcs, the athletics track
Area of a rectangle, parallelogram, triangle, trapezium and the median property; squaring a rectangle
Heron's formula and Brahmagupta's formula for a cyclic 4-gon and their special cases
Area of a circle, sector and segment
End-of-chapter exercises on perimeter and area

concepts.name: Perimeter of shapes and the circumference of a circle
concepts.description: Perimeter of squares, triangles and rectangles; the constant ratio C/D of circumference to diameter and the formula C = 2 pi r.
concepts.idea: Perimeter is the length around a shape; for every circle the circumference divided by the diameter is the same number.
concepts.rule: Square 4a, equilateral triangle 3a, rectangle 2(a + b). For a circle C/D = pi, so C = pi d = 2 pi r.
concepts.example: A circle of radius 7 cm has circumference 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm (using pi = 22/7).

questions.q: Explain why the ratio C/D is the same for circles of every size.
questions.a: Enlarging a circle scales the circumference and diameter by the same factor, just as the perimeter and side of a square scale together (ratio 4 : 1 for every square). So C/D does not change with size.
s: Compares with the fixed perimeter : side ratio of squares or scaling
States that circumference and diameter scale together so C/D is constant

questions.q: Two circles of radius r each pass through the centre of the other. Find the perimeter of the shape formed by the two outer arcs.
questions.a: The triangle formed by the two centres and an intersection point is equilateral, so the angle at each centre inside the other circle is 120 degrees. The outer arc of each circle is 240 degrees, which is 2/3 of the circumference. Total = 2 x (2/3) x 2 pi r = 8 pi r/3.
s: Equilateral triangle gives 60 degree angles, so 120 degrees at each centre
Each outer arc is 2/3 of a circumference

questions.q: Ravi says larger circles have a larger C/D ratio. Evaluate.
questions.a: He is wrong. C/D equals pi for every circle, whatever its size.

questions.q: Describe a home measurement to estimate the C/D ratio of a cotton reel.
questions.a: Measure the diameter D of the reel. Wrap thin thread tightly around it 20 times, unwrap it and measure its length L. Then C/D is about L/(20 D), which should be near 3.14.
s: Wraps thread 20 times and measures L
Computes L/(20D) as the C/D ratio

concepts.name: Pi: approximations, history and irrationality
concepts.description: The number pi as the C/D ratio, its historical approximations and Madhava's series, and why pi is irrational.
concepts.idea: Pi cannot be written as a fraction, so every fraction is only an approximation; better approximations were found by many mathematicians.
concepts.rule: pi is irrational (Lambert, 1761), so pi is not equal to 22/7 although pi is approximately 22/7. Approximations: 3.125 (Mesopotamia), 22/7 and 355/113 (Zu Chongzhi), 3.1416 (Aryabhata, asanna), root 10 (Brahmagupta). Madhava: pi/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7 + ...
concepts.example: 22/7 = 3.142857 is close to pi = 3.14159265... but not equal to it.

questions.q: Explain why we write pi is approximately 22/7 and also pi is not equal to 22/7.
questions.a: 22/7 = 3.142857... repeats, while pi is irrational and its decimal never repeats. The two values are very close but not the same number.
s: 22/7 is a fraction (repeating decimal) but pi is irrational
So 22/7 is only a close approximation

Write 22/7 and 355/113 as decimals (to 6 places) and say which is closer to pi.
The Mesopotamians took pi = 3 + 1/8. Why does a hexagon inside a circle show pi is greater than 3?
questions.a: A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle of radius r has perimeter 6r = 3d, which is less than the circumference. So C > 3d and C/D > 3.
s: Circle is longer than the hexagon, so pi > 3

questions.q: For a circle of radius 1, an inscribed regular hexagon has perimeter 6. Use this and the circumscribed hexagon (perimeter 4 root 3, about 6.93) to trap pi.
questions.a: The circle has circumference 2 pi, and 6 < 2 pi < 4 root 3. Dividing by 2: 3 < pi < 2 root 3, about 3.46.
s: Circumscribed hexagon perimeter about 6.93 gives pi < 3.46

questions.q: Fractions have decimals that terminate or repeat. Since pi is irrational, its decimal
questions.a: never terminates and never repeats

questions.q: Why do decimals of fractions like 1/7 show a pattern but the decimal of pi does not?
questions.a: A fraction has a decimal that ends or repeats. Pi is irrational, so it cannot be written as a fraction and its decimal never repeats.
s: Rational numbers give ending or repeating decimals
Pi is irrational so no repeating pattern

questions.q: Brahmagupta used root 10, about 3.1623, for pi. Compare the errors of root 10 and 22/7 (pi = 3.14159).
questions.a: Root 10 is 3.16228 with error about 0.0207. 22/7 is 3.14286 with error about 0.0013. So 22/7 is more accurate.

questions.q: Nisha says pi is exactly 3.14. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. 3.14 is only an approximation. Pi is irrational and its decimal never ends or repeats.
s: Pi is irrational with a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal

questions.q: Make a sentence whose word lengths give the digits 3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9 of pi.
questions.a: For example "Can I have a large container": the words have 3, 1, 4, 1, 5 and 9 letters.

concepts.name: Arc length, perimeter of a sector and composite shapes
concepts.description: Length of an arc from the angle at the centre, perimeter of sectors and shapes made from arcs, and the athletics track.
concepts.idea: An arc is the fraction theta/360 of the whole circumference.
concepts.rule: Arc length = 2 pi r x theta/360. Semicircle: pi r. Quarter circle: pi r/2. Perimeter of a sector = arc + 2r.
concepts.example: A 60 degree arc of a circle of radius 3.5 cm has length 22/6 = 11/3 cm (pi = 22/7).

questions.q: Path a is one semicircle of radius a on PQ as diameter. Path b + c + d is made of three semicircles on parts of PQ with radii b, c and d that fit end to end along PQ. Show that the two paths have equal length.

questions.a: Perimeter = 8 + 8 + 6 + arc of the semicircle of radius 3 = 22 + (22/7) x 3 = 22 + 66/7, about 31.4 cm.

concepts.name: Areas of rectangles, parallelograms, triangles and trapezia
concepts.description: Area of a rectangle, parallelogram, triangle and trapezium; the median divides a triangle into equal areas; squaring a rectangle.
concepts.idea: Areas are found by cutting and rearranging shapes into rectangles.
concepts.rule: Rectangle ab; parallelogram bh; triangle (1/2)bh; trapezium (1/2)(a + b)h. A median splits a triangle into two triangles of equal area. A square of side root(ab) has the same area as an a by b rectangle.
concepts.example: A triangle with base 10 and height 8 has area 40 square units.

questions.a: The height is sqrt(26^2 - 10^2) = 24 cm (the overhang on each side is (40 - 20)/2 = 10). Area = (1/2)(40 + 20) x 24 = 720 cm^2.

questions.q: Meera says the area of a parallelogram is the product of two adjacent sides. Evaluate.

s: Says the perpendicular height must be used

questions.q: Two rectangles have the same perimeter and the same area. Show that they are congruent.
questions.a: Let the sides be a, b with a + b = s (half the perimeter) and ab = A. Then a and b are the two roots of x^2 - sx + A = 0, so the pair {a, b} is fixed by s and A. Both rectangles have the same two side lengths, so they are congruent.
s: Uses a + b and ab as fixed quantities
Sides are determined as the roots of one equation
So both rectangles have the same sides and are congruent

concepts.name: Heron's formula and Brahmagupta's formula
concepts.description: Area of a triangle from its three sides (Heron) and of a cyclic quadrilateral from its four sides (Brahmagupta), with special cases.
concepts.idea: The area of a triangle can be found from its sides alone, but for a quadrilateral extra information such as being cyclic is needed.
concepts.rule: Heron: s = (a + b + c)/2 and area = sqrt(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)). Brahmagupta: for a cyclic 4-gon s = (a + b + c + d)/2 and area = sqrt((s - a)(s - b)(s - c)(s - d)). Putting d = 0 gives Heron's formula.
concepts.example: Sides 3, 4, 5: s = 6 and area = sqrt(6 x 3 x 2 x 1) = 6.

questions.a: Heron: s = 6, area = sqrt(6 x 3 x 2 x 1) = 6. Since 3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2 the triangle is right-angled and (1/2) x 3 x 4 = 6. The two agree.
s: Right triangle base-height gives 6, so they agree

questions.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides 5, 5, 12, 12. Find its area with Brahmagupta's formula.
Ria says Heron's formula only works for right-angled triangles. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. Heron's formula works for every triangle, as the equilateral and isosceles examples show.

questions.q: Show that Heron's formula is a special case of Brahmagupta's formula.
questions.a: A triangle with sides a, b, c is a cyclic 4-gon whose fourth side d = 0. Then s = (a + b + c)/2, the triangle's semi-perimeter, and (s - d) = s. Brahmagupta's formula becomes sqrt(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)), which is Heron's formula.
s: Treats a triangle as a 4-gon with d = 0

concepts.name: Area of a circle, sector and segment
concepts.description: The formula A = pi r^2 and its justifications; area of a sector and a segment of a circle.
concepts.idea: The area of a circle is proportional to the square of the radius; slicing the circle into sectors and rearranging them gives a parallelogram.
concepts.rule: Area of a circle = pi r^2. Area of a sector with central angle theta degrees = pi r^2 x theta/360. A segment is the region between an arc and its chord.
concepts.example: A circle of radius 7 has area (22/7) x 49 = 154; a 60 degree sector of it has area 154/6 = 77/3.

questions.q: Explain Nilakantha's argument that the area of a circle is pi r^2.
questions.a: Cut the circle into thin slices and rearrange them into a shape close to a parallelogram. Its base is half the circumference, pi r, and its height is the radius r. Area = base x height = pi r^2.
s: Rearranges the slices into a near-parallelogram with base pi r and height r
Area = pi r x r = pi r^2

A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends 90 degrees at the centre. Find the areas of the minor sector and the major sector (pi = 3.14).
questions.a: Circle area = 3.14 x 100 = 314. Minor sector = 314 x 90/360 = 78.5 cm^2. Major sector = 314 - 78.5 = 235.5 cm^2.

questions.q: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius r. The ratio of the area of the square to the area of the circle is
questions.a: 2/pi

questions.q: A chord subtends 60 degrees at the centre of a circle of radius r. Show that the minor segment has area r^2 (pi/6 - root 3/4).
questions.a: The sector has area pi r^2/6. The triangle formed by the two radii and the chord is equilateral with area (root 3/4) r^2. The segment is the sector minus this triangle: r^2 (pi/6 - root 3/4).

questions.q: Two concentric circles have a common centre O. A chord BC of the larger circle of length l touches the smaller circle at A. Show that the area between the circles is pi l^2/4.
questions.a: A is the midpoint of BC (the perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord), so BA = l/2. In the right triangle OAB, R^2 = r^2 + (l/2)^2, so R^2 - r^2 = l^2/4. The area between the circles is pi(R^2 - r^2) = pi l^2/4.
s: OA is perpendicular to BC, so BA = l/2
R^2 - r^2 = (l/2)^2 by the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem

questions.q: Tara says a circle of radius 2r has twice the area of a circle of radius r. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. The area is pi (2r)^2 = 4 pi r^2, which is four times pi r^2.
s: Area is 4 times because it depends on r^2

questions.q: Show that the ratio of the area of an equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle of radius r to the area of the circle is 3 root 3/(4 pi), about 0.413.
questions.a: The side of the inscribed equilateral triangle is r root 3, so its area is (root 3/4)(3r^2) = 3 root 3 r^2/4. Dividing by pi r^2 gives 3 root 3/(4 pi), about 0.413.
s: Side of the triangle is r root 3
